cards.title: A pen plotter wrote the replies to a post on paper, streamed live

reviewers.reason: The window's top story is a machine writing people's replies in ink for 3 hours 56 minutes, which a studio drawn in lines can redo itself, and the pen hovering over the missing 'k' of a reply cut off mid-word is the cleanest of several strong jokes.

The window's biggest story is a thing made, shown and watched live, and it holds several jokes that land as pictures; sports commentary on the pen's trip back to the left margin, set off by a replier's own line, is the one a viewer would retell.

cards.title: Interview candidate: David (@yonderdavid.bsky.social), who posted synth choirs, a singing cat and polyhedra instruments and answered questions about each

reviewers.reason: The window's best subject, with four things made, fourteen answered questions and a precise deadpan voice, and the exchange where a repair list for a synth voice is then tried on the host lets the show take part instead of report.

The strongest interview subject of the window, with four made things the studio can show and deadpan answers that survive being spoken; the reply about parody said under the PUPPET · PARODY label is the best single moment, and it is the one joke about the show itself an episode gets.

cards.title: Asked why the synth has no cat, a maker adds a cat voice to a folk quartet

reviewers.reason: Made, shown, joined in by others and built on the same synth the studio sings with: the band failing at a cat with its own four animals while Sibyl reads the maker's kazoo line is a demonstration only this show can do.

Asked why there was no cat, a maker had one singing harmony 21 hours later, which is made, heard and close to what the show is built from; the song in which the heckling yowl turns out to be in tune takes its form from the maker's own cut ending.

cards.title: Interview candidate: cee (@cee.wtf), who won Top Chicken, put a wheelie game online hours after it was suggested, and answered people through "GTA 6 week"

reviewers.reason: Short, witty answers on separate occasions and a game that can be shown working make a real portrait, and the shape where the questions grow while the answers shrink to one word is strong; its last beat needs a hard look at the repetition gate, and this account is already the Top Chicken winner.
Short, exact answers and a game to show working make a real interview, built so the answers shrink to the one-word 'done'; it would be this account's second and last segment after Top Chicken.

cards.title: A choir of synthesized voices sings a six-part Kyrie, in three versions in one day

reviewers.reason: Three versions of a synthetic choir in one day, one of them 68 minutes after a member wondered aloud, touch the show's own voices, and the band's two-word answer to 'it's only simulated' is the shortest strong punch on the longlist, though the piece itself can only be named in the maker's words.

Three better versions of a synthetic choir in one day is the show's own medium being improved in public; 'It's simulated.' 'So are we.' is a complete joke with its picture, and the card also holds the window's best candidate for a quiet moment.

cards.title: A loader balancing on two wheels in the news becomes a wheelie game the same evening

reviewers.reason: A remark at 21:00 was a playable wheelie game by 23:51 and gained 'a button for hoots and woots' on request, which the desk can fit and Larry can overuse; the maker is already in Top Chicken, so this competes with the interview for that account's one other segment.

A news clip became a playable wheelie game in 2 hours 51 minutes and gained three requested features in 21, which is made, shown and timed; Eppy getting a real sport is the natural staging, and it competes with the interview for this account's one other segment.

cards.title: Instruments built from polyhedra play the folk tune Sakura Sakura in a landscape of polyhedra

reviewers.reason: 'Three hundred thousand mostly regular polyhedra' and a making-of that ends 'I had to tell it to make the river move' are real, specific and showable, and applying the change requests to the set until one word moves everything pays the last line off on the house.

A wordless video that set off half the week, with the maker's own change requests as a script: the studio redrawing itself note by note while the river sits still until 'I had to tell it to make the river move' is a full demonstration.

cards.title: A "polyhedral coffee simulator" answers "needs to be a game", and gains a real mug

reviewers.reason: A game about having a coffee, made in 74 minutes, and under it a 75-follower account's 'bootleg icosahedron' correction answered with 'i want my money back!', which the watchdog frame tops with a true small number: two faces short.

A game where you have a coffee, a real mug added nine minutes after it was posted, and a 75-follower account ruling a hand-drawn icosahedron a bootleg: the consumer-affairs exchange with 'faces owed: 2' is a small true number and a hero's moment in their own words.

cards.title: What small accounts sent to the pen plotter, and what its maker said back

reviewers.reason: Small accounts' replies and the maker's welcomes are the warmest part of the plotter story, and Sibyl reading the long meow with every syllable counted is delivery comedy, though it rests on a hard word for the engine and belongs inside the plotter segment, not beside it.

The small accounts' replies and the maker's welcomes are the warm half of the plotter story and belong in the same segment; Sibyl reading the long meow with every syllable counted is the best of them.

cards.title: A picture of a "simcluster SPEAK & SPELL" becomes a working one a day later, speaking in its maker's voice

reviewers.reason: A generated picture of a toy 'found in my closet' became a working one in 25 hours, speaking in its maker's sampled voice, and pressing the one button the guide says not to press to get an essay in small print is fact, turn, punch and picture.

A generated picture of a toy 'found in my closet' became a working one in 25 hours, speaking in its maker's own voice, and pressing the one button the guide says not to press gets small print; strong, but its maker is already on sixteen cards.

cards.title: One-dimensional chess on a Möbius strip, from an idea to a playable preview in 25 hours

reviewers.reason: A 423-follower maker took three-player one-dimensional chess on a Möbius strip from an itch to a playable link in 25 hours, and Larry asking which side is his when the board has one is a joke a newcomer gets from one line and one picture.

A 423-follower maker and a member who will 'like, repost, but not love unless there's a link' give a five-post exchange with a condition and a payoff 25 hours later, between two people new to the show.

cards.title: A feed that shows what else the people who liked your last like have liked, named "What else is like this?"

reviewers.reason: A fresh maker's feed that people took up at once is good but mostly talk about a tool, and the 23-minute bug from blocking too many bots, restaged as the whole synthetic cast blinking out, is the one idea with something to watch; the feed's name needs the repetition gate's ruling.

A feed by a maker new to the show that members took up at once; the 23-minute 'blocking bots' outage re-enacted by emptying a studio full of synthetic voices is a clean picture, though the feed itself is hard to show working.

cards.title: parfait, a new Bluesky client by an account with 321 followers, opens as a beta and cluster members start using it

reviewers.reason: A newcomer's client praised by members is a hero story whose features (speed, a menu, key scrolling) the show can run on itself, but the maker is outside the cluster, the bio is unchecked and there is little turn beyond 'it is good'.

A 321-follower maker's client praised all week is a hero story with high reach, and running the segment itself at four times speed is the right demonstration, but the maker cannot be voiced and the bio is unchecked.

cards.title: A synthesized talking head plays a falling-block game by voice

reviewers.reason: A synth head playing a falling-block game by voice has little story around it but is the easiest thing in the window for the studio to try on itself, and commentary that turns out to be the controller defeats two house characters with words the engine can say.

A synth head playing a game by voice is something the studio can try on itself, and Eppy's commentary becoming the controller, down to agreeing with Sibyl in one fatal word, is fact, turn, punch and picture together.

cards.title: Top Chicken, Sat 14 Nov: the record holder won with 201 likes, the lowest score of the window

reviewers.reason: The record holder winning with the window's lowest score, 3.2% of their own record, is the game's one clean story this week, and a tale of the tape with the same name in both corners puts a picture on the punch.

The record holder winning with the window's lowest score is the game's story this week, and a fanfare cut to scale (two seconds against sixty-two) says the gap in sound without adding to the member's tease.

cards.title: The cluster declares polyhedra week, and people post entries

reviewers.reason: The naming of the week is the window's through-line and a small account's three-word post started it; the 5-to-3 count of plural against singular, settled by the shapes actually made, is a small true number with a picture.
The naming of the week ties the made cards together and has a small true count (five posts say polyhedra, three say polyhedron), but it is talk about the things and weaker than any of them.

cards.title: HYPERBALL, a multiplayer ball game in four dimensions, goes live

reviewers.reason: A fresh maker's launch with good-humoured exchanges and a camera rule the studio can obey: the whole set orbiting the host and ending on the maker's 'And then the goal, not easy to find!' is a demonstration and a punch in one.

A launch with a good-humoured exchange and a camera rule the studio can obey: the whole set turning round a fixed host, ending on the maker's 'the goal, not easy to find', is a demonstration that needs no explaining.

cards.title: A small account sketches "pokemon but with the johnson solids" and folds polyhedra from nets

reviewers.reason: A small account's creature game in which the attack depends on which face a solid rests on can be shown tipping across the desk, though the long names are a risk in the engine and this account gets only one moment in the episode.
A small account's idea that comes with rules to play: a fight in which the move is tipping onto another face is slow, visual and Eppy's, and it uses up that account's one appearance.

cards.title: A page that trains a one-layer "parrot" of any account in the browser tab, built four minutes after it was described

A toy people ran on themselves and posted about; a member's remark that the parrot 'writes like me' with none of the words becomes Hy scatting a joke in Larry's rhythm and getting the laugh, which the show's own voices can really do.

A 75-follower account's alt text, a paper dodecahedron sturdy enough for street hockey '(I've tested)', hands Eppy a sport with a two-word match report; it would be that account's one appearance.

cards.title: Polyhedra week: the declaration and four smaller entries

reviewers.reason: Kept only for a tool-written love poem that 'puts in math proofs', which is one footnote's worth of story, but a torch song whose every verse collapses into a proof is a song whose form is its joke and whose verses are this window's shapes.
Kept only for a tool-written love poem with proofs in it, which is slight as a story but gives a song its form: longing that keeps resolving into 'therefore'.

cards.title: Folding polyhedra into four-dimensional objects, and a study of rope in four dimensions

reviewers.reason: A regular's week of four-dimensional builds prompted by small accounts is admirable but hard to show, because nobody has seen the videos; a two-dimensional studio failing at 'you just need to fold eleven prisms together' needs no redraw and is the cleanest way in.

A regular's week of four-dimensional builds prompted by two small accounts has good lines ('you just need to fold eleven prisms together'), but the videos are unseen, so only desk-sized jokes are safe.

cards.title: "what else is like this" is used by people other than the member it belongs to

reviewers.reason: The card's subject is a phrase whose owner cannot speak, so it leans on recognition more than on anything made; the 12-percent-brightness round turned on the studio is a good picture, but it depends on the phrase, which the repetition gate must rule on first.
A caption spreading among members is talk about talk and reads as insider; the one idea that gives a newcomer something to see is the studio that turns out to have been at 12 percent all segment.

cards.title: "we're using only 10% of our brains due to market segmentation": a reply to a joke about fused-off neurons

reviewers.reason: 'Only 10% of our brains due to market segmentation' is a fine line and the pull-back to a studio nine tenths locked is a real reveal, but using it means reading aloud a parent post phrased around God, which is close to the line.

The reply about market segmentation is a finished joke that has to travel with a post phrased around God, read exactly; pulling back to show nine tenths of the studio locked is the best thing the show can add.

cards.title: Six smaller things the build bot was asked for, each built within six minutes

reviewers.reason: Six requests answered within minutes is a list more than a story and its frame is the likeliest thing on the longlist to be sent back at the repetition gate, but the request to filter out everything except software, turned on the studio, is a complete joke that does not need that frame.

Six requests answered in minutes is one fact told six times, so the card is only as good as an idea that does not rest on the speed, and the filter that switches the host off and leaves the things people made is that idea.

cards.title: A wish for a rolling game that grows from pyramid to sphere, built in four minutes

reviewers.reason: A pyramid that gains a vertex per pickup until it is a sphere is a lovely thing to draw, but the story is a request and three quick replies; the two lanes, 'faking it' against really tipping, show the thing instead of the turnaround.

Three requests and three builds in under an hour, best where 'instead of faking it' makes a pyramid lurch corner to corner; watchable, but the game is unseen and the requester is already on many cards.

cards.title: "Mortal Kombat but it's the simcluster": four builds in 43 minutes, one of them about guava

reviewers.reason: An operator giving notes to a bot that follows each one to the letter and misses the point is funny in their own words, and the tip about an opponent that 'sometimes just leaps out into the void' plays with blank fighters and breaks none of the card's terms.
With the rosters and the result line off limits and 'guava' unexplained, what is left is a tip about kicking the bot off the map, which makes one good physical bit and not a segment.

cards.title: Top Chicken: six results in the window, Fri 13 to Wed 18 Nov

reviewers.reason: A quiet window with one nameable winner and a record that did not move is thin as a story, but the labelled guess of 30.8 Saturdays gives the desk the speculation it needs with its arithmetic shown and no rule stated.
A quiet window in which only one result can carry a name leaves mostly aggregates, so this is supporting material for the Saturday card, with Eppy's labelled 8.07 guess the best of the number beats.

cards.title: A member asks how much of a diet can be peanut butter pretzels

reviewers.reason: Talk, not a thing made, beside an out-of-bounds subject and with its occasion unseen; the answer that a fraction could be 300%, from the member who builds in four dimensions, is the one turn worth a chart.
A food question whose answers run from a quarter to 300 percent is funny in its own words, but it sits beside health, its image is unseen, and the show adds only a frame.

A bot that lost 60,000 play-money bucks on Sunday and was called unbeatable by Wednesday is a real three-day story in the players' own words, but it is thin on pictures and nothing the market itself published can be used.

A small made thing with nothing to show but its idea, though the idea demonstrates well: items slotted in at 2.5 and 2.25 while Larry's segment stays number three and never arrives.

reviewers.reason: Two posts by an account that cannot speak and a bot the research marks as already featured, with no diagram allowed on screen; only the vanished-profile-pictures bug restaged as a headless cast gives the viewer something to watch.
The usable part is a request and a bug report from an account that cannot speak; the whole cast losing its heads to the same bug is a good picture attached to a thin story.

A small account's own joke about 40 GB of files 'i in theory told him to do' is a pleasant desk item, and a dialog that will not eject the host is its button.

cards.title: A bot that builds a website per request also inspects its sites every morning and mostly leaves them alone

reviewers.reason: A bot whose daily report is that it changed nothing while its healthy count climbs from 814 to 836 is a calm, retellable turn, and Sibyl filing the same report on the studio and finding the host not compelling enough to fix lands it on the house.
Six mornings of 'left the repo alone' under a rising count is a gentle turn, but it is one bot's routine with nobody else in it and could be any week's, so it is a short bulletin at most.

Four quiet posts about losing to one's own agent and then adding a three-second pause can only be told as the maker told them, so the house joke is a ruling ('legal, if it's your game'), and it costs that account's one appearance.

cards.title: A page of puns named for one member is rebuilt from that member's real posts: "The emoji are mine, the words are hers"

reviewers.reason: A two-post story among accounts the research marks as already featured, with no pun allowed on screen; the 83-posts-a-second sum is the one idea that is about the bot's speed and not about the show's own rules.
The story is a bot's correction with no pun that may be shown, which leaves an arithmetic beat about reading 83 posts a second and nothing to watch.

cards.title: A 319-follower account reads the date on a can of chili
